steps.observation: Work on this for 30 seconds; do not stop early. Explain the difference between RNA and DNA.

steps.action:
Here are the key differences between DNA and RNA:

1. Sugar backbone  
   • DNA contains deoxyribose (lacks an –OH group on the 2′ carbon)  
   • RNA contains ribose (has an –OH group on the 2′ carbon)

2. Nitrogenous bases  
   • DNA uses adenine (A), guanine (G), cytosine (C) and thymine (T)  
   • RNA uses A, G, C and uracil (U) instead of thymine

3. Strand structure  
   • DNA is typically double-stranded, forming a double helix  
   • RNA is usually single-stranded and can fold into complex 3D shapes

4. Function  
   • DNA stores and transmits genetic information in cells and across generations  
   • RNA converts that genetic information into proteins (mRNA), forms part of ribosomes (rRNA), and helps carry amino acids (tRNA), among other roles

5. Stability and lifespan  
   • DNA is chemically more stable—suited for long-term storage  
   • RNA is more prone to hydrolysis (because of its 2′-OH), so it’s generally shorter-lived

6. Cellular location  
   • In eukaryotes, DNA resides mainly in the nucleus (and mitochondria/chloroplasts)  
   • RNA is synthesized in the nucleus but functions in the cytoplasm (and sometimes in organelles)

Together, these differences allow DNA to serve as the long-term genetic archive and RNA to act as a versatile, transient messenger and functional molecule in gene expression.
